No column or cell states hours. Both lesson code blocks match the source character-for-character.
git show stage-0:docs/team/sprint-example.md line 39, under '## Retrospective' (line 35): '- Hành động cho sprint sau: mỗi việc lớn hơn 3 điểm phải có hai người đọc code.'

Scrum Guide (November 2020), Product Backlog: 'Product Backlog refinement is ... an ongoing activity to add details, such as a description, order, and size. Attributes often vary with the domain of work. The Developers who will be doing the work are responsible for the sizing.' Scrum Definition: 'Various processes, techniques and methods can be employed within the framework.' Fetched page summary reported no mention of 'story points' or any estimation technique (absence taken from the WebFetch summary, not a verbatim search).

The lesson's working definition of its own vocab term, taken from outline item 1 and misconception 1. The pinned Scrum Guide 2020 does not define story points, so no pinned document can confirm or contradict it; accepted as definitional. The extra sentence about what 'effort' contains is not covered by this claim (see issue on section 4).

Ledger and outline item 3 say 'usually easier and more consistent'. Section 4 drops the hedge and adds an unsourced empirical causal claim: 'People are much more consistent at comparing than at predicting durations, so the numbers agree more often and change less from person to person.' Summary line 3 also drops 'usually'. No pinned doc in versions.yaml supports 'much more consistent'.
claim_verdicts.suggested_text: Comparing a story with ones the team already knows is usually easier than predicting its hours, and teammates' answers usually agree more closely.

issues.text: Comparative, unconditional empirical claim with no source; stronger than the ledger's 'usually' (claim 5). Same unhedged form repeated in summary line 3: 'Comparing a story with known ones is easier and more consistent than predicting its hours.'
issues.quote: People are much more consistent at comparing than at predicting durations, so the numbers agree more often and change less from person to person.
issues.fix: Replace the section 4 sentence with: 'Comparing is usually easier than predicting, so teammates' numbers usually agree more closely.' Change summary line 3 to: 'Comparing a story with known ones is usually easier and more consistent than predicting its hours.'

issues.text: Unlisted claim: the lesson asserts what 'effort' consists of, which contradicts its own 'whatever effort means to that team' and is not in the claims ledger.
issues.quote: whatever "effort" means to that team: time, complexity, risk and unknowns all mixed together.
issues.fix: Either cut after 'whatever "effort" means to that team.' or hedge it: 'for many teams, a mix of time, complexity and unknowns.' If kept, add it to claims as kind opinion.

issues.text: Diagram labels contradict the ratio the lesson defines. Text: a 3-point story is about three times a 1-point story, so a 2 should be about twice the reference. Diagram maps 'a bit bigger' to 2, teaching an inconsistent scale in the lesson whose core concept is that ratio.
issues.fix: Change the edge label to 'about twice' : `C -->|about twice| B[2]`. Diagrams are not repo code, so this edit is free.

issues.text: The prose never walks through the diagram. The three arrows (about the same -> 1, about twice -> 2, about three times -> 3) and the 'reference' node are not narrated; the prose never uses the words 'reference story'. The decision node asks 'bigger or smaller?' but only bigger branches exist, so I cannot tell what to do with a story smaller than the bug fix.
issues.fix: Add two sentences before 'Relative estimates are easier...': 'Start from a reference story the team knows, such as the small bug fix at 1. Ask whether the new story is about the same, about twice or about three times as big, and give it 1, 2 or 3.' Or relabel the node 'how much bigger?'.

issues.text: The third developer's objection (it depends who does it and how the code looks today) is never answered. I cannot tell whether comparing with the bug fix removes that problem or just hides it.
issues.quote: a third says it depends who does it and how the order screen code looks today
issues.fix: Add one sentence in section 4 after 'only needs a comparison with things the team has already done' saying that the comparison does not depend on which person picks the story up, because the size belongs to the story, not the person.

issues.text: The reference story is 'a small bug fix', but from the user-story lesson a story is 'As a..., I want...'. The Sprint 14 table mixes a bug fix with features and the prose calls them 'items' and 'stories' interchangeably. I paused wondering whether a bug fix counts as a story that gets points.
issues.quote: a story the team knows well and uses as a yardstick, such as a small bug fix sized at 1
issues.fix: Add one clause in section 5 after 'The wrong-total bug is the smallest, at 1': 'every backlog item, bug fixes included, gets a number on the same scale.'

issues.text: In the expected result, step numbers and point values are both bare numbers, so '1 — the wrong-total fix (1)' and '2 — any number from 1 to 3' read ambiguously. I had to re-read to see which '1' and '2' are steps.
issues.quote: Expected result: 1 — the wrong-total fix (1); then the two items at 2;
issues.fix: Write 'Step 1:', 'Step 2:', 'Step 3:' instead of '1 —', '2 —', '3 —' in the expected result.

issues.text: q1: the correct option is almost a verbatim copy of section 4's first sentence, so it can be matched without understanding.
issues.quote: A story's size compared with the team's other stories
issues.fix: Rephrase option a, e.g. 'How big a story is next to stories the team has already sized'.

issues.text: q2: the correct option echoes section 4's 'each compares it with its own earlier work' nearly word for word; option d is ruled out by the table at a glance, leaving an easy pick.
issues.quote: False, because each team compares stories with its own earlier work.
issues.fix: Reword option c, e.g. 'False, because a point only has meaning on the scale of the team that gave it.'

issues.text: q4: the correct option is clearly the longest and the only one naming two faults, so it can be guessed by length.
issues.quote: The manager read points as hours and compared two teams' separate scales
issues.fix: Lengthen the distractors to similar size, e.g. b: 'Team B works about half as fast as Team A and should speed up'.

skipped_steps: Section 4 diagram: arrows about the same/about twice/about three times -> 1/2/3 and the 'smaller' branch are never explained in prose.
Section 2 -> 4: the 'depends who does it' objection is raised but not resolved.
